content.title: About
content.content: Provolone is a semi‑hard Italian cheese made from cow’s milk, known for its mild nutty flavor and slightly sharp aroma. Sliced provolone is commonly used in sandwiches, salads, casseroles, and hot dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Provolone is named after the Italian town of Provola, where it was first produced in the 19th century.
The cheese is aged from 2 to 12 months; longer aging yields a stronger taste.
Traditionally it is made from whole milk without added cream.
Provolone melts well, often replacing mozzarella in baked dishes.
In Italy it is frequently served thinly sliced with ham and olives.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Calcium in provolone supports strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Good source of protein
items.content: The cheese provides high‑quality animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Provolone contains vitamins B2, B12 and niacin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains polyunsaturated fats
items.content: Beneficial fats help maintain cardiovascular health.

items.title: Probiotic properties
items.content: Fermentation promotes beneficial bacteria that support gut microbiota.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to casein or lactose may react to provolone.

items.title: High salt content
items.content: The cheese is often salty; those with hypertension should monitor intake.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Because of its fat content, provolone is calorie‑dense; moderation is key for weight control.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Elevated sodium can affect kidney function in susceptible individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sliced provolone is convenient for adding to sandwiches, salads, pizza and casseroles. It can be melted into sauces, used in hot paninis, or served as a snack with olives and wine.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store provolone in its original packaging or tightly wrapped in plastic film in the refrigerator at 1‑4 °C. It typically lasts 2‑3 weeks after opening. Discard if mold or off‑odors develop.
